text: You walk into your bank, hoping to see a familiar face, maybe even the teller who helped you last time. A little consistency would be nice.
But almost always, it's a completely new person behind the counter. You wonder, 'Where did the last one go? Do they just keep hiring?'
It feels like endless turnover or bad luck. You're always starting fresh, repeating your request, wishing for some continuity.
This constant rotation is actually a deliberate strategy. Banks cross-train staff in many roles and move them between branches, building a resilient system.
If a teller is sick or moves roles, another trained person steps right in. Your banking experience stays seamless, even if the face changes.
So while you might miss a personal connection, you're seeing a robust system. It ensures your money is always accessible and bank operations never stop.
